name_en: Narae — seven vegetables and fried tofu dressed in a sweet vinegar
summary_ja: 大根、にんじん、油揚げなど7つの食材を三杯酢で和える精進料理由来の一品。もとは奈良漬けが加わっていたことから「奈良和え」と呼んだのがなまったとされ、法事や彼岸に供されてきたという。
summary_en: Seven ingredients — daikon, carrot, fried tofu, and more — are dressed in a three-part vinegar, a dish said to trace back to shojin temple cooking. Its name is thought to be a slurring of Nara-ae, from when Nara pickles were once part of the mix, and it has been served at memorial services and equinox observances.
source_title: ならえ 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Yubeshi — yuzu peel simmered thick in sugar and soy sauce
summary_ja: ゆずの皮を刻み、砂糖と醤油でとろみが出るまで甘辛く煮詰める保存食。ゆず生産量が全国有数の那賀町相生地区では、11月ごろゆずが完熟する時期にじっくり仕込み、副食やお茶請けにするという。
summary_en: Yuzu peel is chopped and simmered down sweet and salty in sugar and soy sauce until thick, into a preserved side dish. In the Aioi district of Naka Town, among the country's leading yuzu-growing areas, it is said to be slow-cooked when the fruit ripens around November, then eaten as a side dish or with tea.
source_title: ゆべし 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Denbu — kintoki beans and root vegetables simmered sweet and salty
summary_ja: 下ゆでした金時豆や黒豆を大根やごぼうなどの根菜と煮込み、醤油と砂糖で甘辛く仕上げる五目豆風の一品。「まめに働いて暮らせるように」との願いを込め、正月や棟上げ式などの祝い膳に加えられるという。
summary_en: Parboiled kintoki or black beans are simmered with root vegetables like daikon and burdock, then finished sweet and salty in soy sauce and sugar. Said to be added to New Year and house-raising feasts as a wish for a hardworking, diligent life, playing on the word for beans, mame, which also means diligence.
source_title: でんぶ 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Tokushima imomochi — sweet potato dough wrapped around red bean paste
summary_ja: ゆでたさつまいももち粉でペースト状にした生地であんを包み、きな粉をまぶす餅菓子。19世紀後半に鳴門にさつまいもが伝わって以降、手に入りやすい甘みとして各家庭で広まったとされる。
summary_en: Boiled sweet potato is blended with glutinous rice flour into a paste, wrapped around red bean paste, and dusted with roasted soybean flour. Said to have spread widely once sweet potato reached Naruto in the late 19th century, offering an affordable sweetness for ordinary households.
source_title: いももち 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Awa no itokoni — dried sweet potato slowly simmered with red beans
summary_ja: 一度ゆでてから干した「ゆで干し」のさつまいもを水で戻し、小豆と弱火で2時間ほど炊き合わせる。冬に乾物づくりが盛んな徳島らしく、うま味が凝縮した干し芋を使う体の温まる副菜とされる。
summary_en: Sweet potato that has been boiled then dried — yude-boshi style — is rehydrated and simmered slowly with red beans for about two hours over low heat. Fitting for a region where drying vegetables is common in winter, it is said to be a warming side dish built on the concentrated flavor of dried sweet potato.
source_title: 阿波のいとこ煮 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Zukigashi — boiled taro stems dressed in a sweet-vinegar dressing
summary_ja: 里芋の一種ヤツガシラの葉柄「ずいき」をゆでて、砂糖や醤油、柚子酢を合わせた酢で和える。ゆでると黒ずむずいきが酢に触れて鮮やかな赤に変わり、しゃきしゃきとした食感を楽しむ一品という。
summary_en: Zuiki — the stem of yatsugashira, a variety of taro — is boiled and dressed in a sweet vinegar mixed with soy sauce and yuzu vinegar. Said to be prized for its crisp texture, the stem turns a dull black when boiled but flushes a vivid red once dressed in vinegar.
source_title: ずきがし 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Iya no decomawashi — potato, tofu, and konjac skewered and grilled with miso
summary_ja: 小ぶりのじゃがいも、そば団子、岩豆腐、丸こんにゃくを串に刺し、囲炉裏でぐるぐる回しながら味噌だれで焼く祖谷地方の郷土料理。串を回す様子が人形浄瑠璃の木偶人形に似ることから名がついたという。
summary_en: Small potatoes, buckwheat dumplings, stone tofu, and whole konjac are skewered and grilled over a hearth with a miso glaze, turned round and round — a specialty of the Iya valley. Said to take its name from the way turning the skewer resembles the head-turning motion of a deku bunraku puppet.
source_title: 祖谷のでこまわし 徳島県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
